title: OpenAI ChatCompletions parity layer: structured-output enforcement, streaming backpressure, and tool-call signal mapping
creator: Aarya Patel
description: Create a parity/adaptation layer so Redwood's API can accept and respond to OpenAI Chat Completions (v1) shaped requests and streaming responses while preserving Redwood semantics for structured outputs and function/tool calls. This ticket focuses on three pain points: 1) streaming delta vs token semantics and backpressure/flow-control, 2) mapping OpenAI's function_call signals into Redwood's structured call lifecycles (partial args streaming, final call), and 3) enforcing structured output schemas (JSON/blocks) when clients rely on ChatCompletions behaviors.
background: Multiple customers have integrations built on OpenAI ChatCompletions shape and expect: streaming 'delta' events, a single final 'content' payload, or function_call subsequences emitted in-stream.

Existing compatibility work handled basic request/response mapping but did not fully cover: incremental function_call arg streaming, strict structured output enforcement, or robust backpressure leading to head-of-line blocking under high concurrency.

This ticket consolidates learnings from prior shims and implements a canonical proxy that: normalizes request fields, converts streaming events to Redwood event stream format, and introduces flow-control to protect runtime tail latency SLOs.
acceptance_criteria: Proxy accepts OpenAI ChatCompletions request body and returns Redwood-compatible streaming SSE/HTTP chunk stream with identical content ordering for non-function flows.

Partial function_call argument chunks from stream are converted to delta fragments under a single function invocation id and recomposed server-side; final function_call triggers one call to the function hook with full args.

When a client requests a structured output schema (json_schema or output_format header), the proxy enforces schema via server-side validation and returns a structured field in the final event; schema validation failures produce a clear 'structured_validation' error event in the stream.

Backpressure: proxy implements token-based flow-control per-connection configurable by route; under heavy load it applies token-window throttling and responds with 'retry-after' or 'throttled' event without dropping active requests.
Comprehensive unit and integration tests cover: canonical role mapping, system instruction preservation, function_call partials, streaming reconnect semantics, and rate-limit behavior.
tasks: Design: define canonical mapping table between OpenAI ChatCompletions fields and Redwood fields (roles, messages, name -> tool mapping).
Prototype: streaming proxy that converts OpenAI 'delta' chunks to Redwood stream events and preserves ordering.
Function-call reassembly: implement incremental arg buffering keyed by (conversation_id, function_call_id) and finalize to single function invocation.
Schema enforcement: integrate JSON Schema validator for structured outputs and produce validation events.
Backpressure: implement per-connection token window, metrics for window utilization, and adaptive throttling policy.
Testing: build a harness that simulates intermittent streaming (split tokens, partial function args) and validates final reconstructed payloads.
Docs & UX: add compatibility guide page and sample client snippets showing how to translate OpenAI streaming into Redwood SDK usage.
Review & Rollout: staged rollout behind feature flag, canary traffic at 5% then 25% before global.
notes: Trade-offs considered: server-side reassembly simplifies clients but increases memory for long-running partial function args; we cap buffered size and fall back to error with instructions to use chunked uploads for large payloads.

We considered preserving OpenAI's 'role' and 'name' verbatim. Instead we canonicalize roles to 'system/user/assistant/tool' and map 'name' to tool id when present to avoid ambiguity in downstream metrics and routing.

To avoid double-emit of final content, the stream translator will suppress OpenAI's final 'content' if the same tokens have already been emitted as deltas; final aggregate event includes provenance header.
risks: Reassembly state increases memory pressure for high-concurrency customers using function_call streaming with large nested args.

Behavior divergence: clients that rely on OpenAI-specific quirks (e.g., multiple function_call objects emitted) may observe different ordering; we will document differences and provide a compatibility mode that preserves original emit ordering at cost to scaling.
Schema enforcement could lead to increased user-visible errors for previously permissive flows; we will gate enforcement behind an opt-in request flag.
implementation_summary: Phase 1 (spike): build minimal translator that accepts OpenAI request, rewrites role/name, streams deltas as events. (done)
Phase 2: add incremental function_call buffering and finalize-to-hook logic; add basic JSON Schema checks for structured outputs. (in progress)
Phase 3: integrate backpressure controls, add metrics & observability, tests, and rollout. (planned)
